newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends up after six month high seen.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends up after six month high seen.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended sharply higher Wednesday, in line with LME copper, extending the four month old recovery in the red metal's price.

"The price action has been impressive and combined with the gains in other base metals prices recently, suggests that economic growth in Europe and Japan may be reviving faster than expected," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
"In copper's case the LME stock builds in the past three months look to have reflected the wide backwardation in the prompt market rather than any mounting supply surplus."
COMEX March copper ended up 2.40 cents at 112.00 cents a pound, after seeing a new six month high intraday at 112.80 cents.

The momentum of latest leg of uptrend since late 1996 remains positive, analysts said, but the nine-day RSI (relative strength indicator) ended above 70 pct Wednesday, suggesting the market may again be becoming temporarily overbought.
COMEX copper open interest rose 1,076 lots Tuesday to 55,076 contracts.

The COMEX March/May spread widened to around 3.95 cents, from 3.60 cents Tuesday, while in London the LME cash-to-three month spread edged out to $74.00 a tonne from a two month low around $5.7.00 a tonne Tuesday.

Although the LME backwardation is well below its recent peak of more than $300, traders said they expected the prompt market to tighten again soon as seasonal demand began to be felt in the April dates.
((-- Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1640))
